interpretation.diagram_classification: Wheel diagram (rota), probably calendrical or cosmological-temporal; unlabelled
interpretation.interpretation: The diagram shows a wheel with a green outer rim, a small central hub and twelve spokes. The spokes are in alternating colours (green, beige, salmon-pink). The twelve-fold division suggests a division of the year into twelve months, or of the day into twelve hours, or a zodiacal scheme. This is only a possible reading. The diagram carries no label, so the exact subject cannot be determined. It may equally be a purely schematic or illustrative wheel of the kind used in computistic, natural-philosophical or theological treatises. The text visible in the background is show-through from the other side of the parchment and is not part of the diagram.
interpretation.evidence: The diagram has no transcribed text, so the interpretation rests only on visible features: the concentric structure (rim, hub, spokes), the count of twelve evenly spaced spokes (Step 1 lists twelve spoke entries, from 12 o'clock round to 11 o'clock), and the colour alternation. Step 1 is consistent with this reading. One small point: the 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock spokes are bicoloured or doubled, and Step 1 describes them only briefly. Without labels, any calendrical, zodiacal or cosmological identification is speculative, so certainty is low. No source is named, because none can be confidently linked to this unlabelled wheel.
